What I Learned When I Inherited a Flagship Application Almost No One Used Cedric Deal 6 min read · Just now -- Listen Share When was the last time you abandoned a tool because using it just felt like too much work? Not because it was broken. Not because it lacked the feature you needed. You gave up because getting what you wanted out of it cost more effort than the thing was worth. That experience has a name. It’s usability, and it is one of the most consequential ideas in software that most of the people building software have never formally encountered. Usability is not how a product looks. It is not the color palette, the icon set, or whether the dashboard feels modern. Usability is whether a real person, doing real work, under real time pressure, can accomplish what they came to accomplish. Without a manual. Without a training session. Without calling the one colleague who figured it out. That distinction sounds academic until it costs you a program. The Program I Inherited I spent most of my career in national security, in environments where the technology tended to be serious and the stakes tended to be real.
